ai.definition: Neuralink is a theoretical technology that envisions the future of artificial intelligence by merging human brains directly with AI through advanced neural implants.
ai.howItWorks: Microchips are embedded into the brain to enable direct interaction and communication between human neural processes and AI systems, potentially enhancing cognitive abilities or creating new forms of brain-computer interfaces.
ai.problemSolved: Current limitations in human-AI integration; potential for overcoming physical barriers that limit current BCI technologies.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves the development and production of microchips with high precision to ensure safe and effective embedding into the brain, along with the creation of biocompatible materials and surgical techniques.
ai.buildProcess: Involves extensive research in neuroscience, material science, and electronics. The build process includes chip design, fabrication, testing, and refinement for safety and efficacy.
ai.costDrivers: High research and development costs, specialized equipment, rigorous testing, and regulatory compliance. Long-term costs could be driven by the need for continuous updates to technology as AI evolves.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Theoretical concept with significant potential but currently in early stages of development; requires substantial validation before reaching practical application.
ai.regulation: High regulatory barriers due to ethical concerns, safety issues, and the complexity of integrating technology into the human body. Requires comprehensive oversight from multiple regulatory bodies.
ai.risks: Ethical concerns, safety risks (infection, rejection), technical challenges in ensuring seamless integration with AI systems, and long-term health impacts are significant hurdles.
ai.profitability: Theoretical at this stage; potential for high profitability if successful but dependent on overcoming numerous technical and regulatory obstacles.
ai.futureDevelopment: Potential for advancements in miniaturization of chips, improvements in biocompatibility, and enhanced AI algorithms to better interact with human neural processes. Continued research into long-term safety and efficacy is crucial.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units would draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and precise microfabrication techniques.

glossary.def: A device embedded in the brain that can interface with neural circuits.
Technology that enables direct communication between a human brain and an external computer system or AI.
The hypothetical state of intelligence far surpassing the cognitive abilities of any human, often associated with advanced AI systems.

subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: the sensor that sits in brain tissue and picks up the electrical spikes of individual neurons.
parts: flexible polymer threads or rigid silicon shanks

subsystems.name: Implant electronics
subsystems.role: amplifies, digitises and packetises neural signals inside the skull.

subsystems.name: Hermetic enclosure
subsystems.role: keeps salty body fluid away from electronics for years.

subsystems.name: Surgical system
subsystems.role: places electrodes without tearing blood vessels on the brain surface.

subsystems.name: Decoder software
subsystems.role: turns firing patterns into intent — cursor movement, speech or keystrokes.

subsystems.name: Power and telemetry
subsystems.role: links the implant to an external unit with no wire through the skin.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode geometry
buildSteps.detail: Channel count, thread stiffness and site spacing are chosen so the array reaches the right neurons without slicing vessels.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the array
buildSteps.detail: Thin-film metal traces are patterned on a polymer or silicon wafer and etched into threads with electrode sites at the tips.

buildSteps.title: Package the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The chip is sealed in a hermetic case, with only the threads emerging, and tested for leaks under pressure and heat cycling.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Arrays are implanted in animal models to measure signal quality and how scar tissue forms around them over months and years.

buildSteps.title: Implant in surgery
buildSteps.detail: A robot or neurosurgeon opens a small hole in the skull, inserts the threads into cortex at a chosen depth, and closes the dura and skin.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the decoder
buildSteps.detail: The user imagines movements or speech while software learns which firing patterns map to which intent.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Decoded intent drives a cursor, robotic arm or speech synthesiser, and feedback helps the decoder keep improving.

buildSteps.title: Monitor for years
buildSteps.detail: Signal quality is tracked as the brain's immune response gradually coats the electrodes.

prerequisites.why: arrays work for months to a few years in humans; long-term stability is still the main limit.
sealed implants such as cochlear and deep-brain stimulators exist, but not with over a thousand exposed channels.
raw neural data cannot stream through the skull at full rate, so much processing must happen on the implant.
research systems let paralysed people type or control arms, but calibration is slow and drifts over time.
inserting hundreds of flexible threads quickly and safely is beyond steady human hands.

pathway.milestone: small clinical trials where implants let paralysed volunteers move a cursor or control a computer
pathway.unlocks: evidence that the interface works in people.

pathway.milestone: higher channel counts and implants that last many years without signal loss
pathway.unlocks: faster typing, richer speech decoding and control of prosthetic limbs.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval for specific medical indications such as communication in paralysis
pathway.unlocks: routine clinical use, which drives down cost and improves reliability.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional implants that also write into neural circuits
pathway.unlocks: possible treatment of blindness, epilepsy or depression — and, far more speculatively, augmentation of healthy brains.

pathway.milestone: high-bandwidth thought-level exchange with AI systems
pathway.unlocks: unknown; bandwidth, safety and consent questions are unresolved and may be unsolvable.
